question:
A charge of 1 C flows from a 100-V outlet through a 100-W light bulb each second. How much work is done each second by this electrical source?
Is the correct answer "100 joules"?

claims.text: Voltage is energy per unit charge, so the work done on a charge is W = qV.
With q = 1 C and V = 100 V, the work done is 100 J.
A 100 W bulb uses 100 J each second.
The work per second computed from W = qV matches the power rating of the bulb.
The two methods, W = qV and W = Pt, agree with each other.
The source's work might differ from the energy dissipated in the bulb.
For an ideal source with negligible internal resistance, the energy supplied equals the energy dissipated by the bulb.
No other plausible numerical value arises from the given data, so there is no competing answer.
